title: The mood just split from the market

lines: What Americans now expect prices to rise over the next year — the lowest reading in months.
It fell about a full point in a single month.
One of the sharpest drops in the University of Michigan survey this year.
Same week the stock market had its worst week in over a year,
households actually felt better — sentiment hit a three-month high.
what people expect prices to do shapes wages, spending, and what the Fed does to your mortgage and card rate.
Wall Street panicked while Main Street exhaled. The trading floor and the kitchen table just split.
Does 3.7% match what you expect your bills to do next year?

source_line: Source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, final November 2026 (released Nov. 20)
caption:
Wall Street just had its worst week in over a year — but regular households got more hopeful about their own money, not less.

In the University of Michigan's final November survey, Americans said they expect prices to rise about 3.7% over the next year — down roughly a full point from the month before, one of the sharpest drops of 2026. Consumer sentiment rose to a three-month high in the same report (University of Michigan, released Nov. 20).

Why it matters for you: inflation expectations are a little self-fulfilling. What people expect prices to do shapes what they'll pay, the raises they ask for, and what the Fed does to the rates on your mortgage and credit card.

My take: Wall Street panicked while Main Street exhaled — the trading floor and the kitchen table told two different stories in the same week.
